description: Tengo un título de Ingeniero Químico y Maestría en Nanotecnología. Dentro de mis fuertes principales está el modelado matemático, la investigación científica, el análisis de datos y modelado básico en Python. Busco personas con experiencia en: Programación, Desarrollo de Aplicaciones Móviles, consumo de APIs y desarrollo de modelos de inteligencia artificial.
summary:
Our team, SIMON, consists of Luis Ibarra, Gilka Puente, David Moreno, Ángel Cárdenas, Kimberly Reyes, and Miguel Briseño.

Our selected challenge is Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots. Our objective is to develop a methodology for harmonizing active fire detection data from both satellite instruments, improving their consistency and comparability.

We propose developing a web-based tool that allows users to access, visualize, and utilize harmonized hotspot data. Our approach will involve exploring statistical and computational techniques for data integration, using Durango, Mexico, as a pilot region.

We will use publicly available satellite data from NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS) and Python for data processing, analysis, and implementation of the harmonization methodology.

Our team aims to compete for the Best Use of Data global award by making satellite data more accessible and useful through an innovative application for active fire monitoring. e-mail.
details:
Our project, SIMON, allows to represent the NASA's FIRMS database in a user friendly Website to track Hot Spot tendencies in a selected area of interest.

The SIMON website provides comprehensible information such as: a Burning Calendar, tracking the Hot Spot detection for the selected region of interest; Dashboard analytics, presenting different variable charts and analytics for the most representative FIRMS variables.

SIMON also include a harmonization module that allows to escalate MODIS lectures to VIIRS, the methodology is based in reducing the resolution differences by defining a new unit: "cellday", which aggregate satellite detection in 5 km x 5 km grid. And then, we use a proportional model to harmonize data, and giving continuity to the full dataset of detentions.

This project helps authorities offer timely responses and create prevention plans. We expect this project helps to preserve important historical data that might support the study of fire activity.

We used technologies such as React, Python, Pandas, among others.
